scope: memory layout, aliasing, lifetime and identity-relevant observations inside the five admitted subregions only

writer_memory_model.aliasing_analysis: Receiver (ECX) and record (arg) are caller-supplied. In all four admitted callsites the receiver is an object pointer from a caller field (R2: [caller+0x18]; R3/R4: [caller+4]; R5: [caller+4] freshly created) while the record is either a caller frame slot (R2/R3/R4: &F+0x3C) or a callee-returned pointer (R5). Frame slot vs heap object field: disjoint. No in-window path can pass receiver==record.
writer_memory_model.lifetime: Writer reads the record fully before returning; R2/R3/R4 then pass the SAME buffer region's base (&F+0x18) to 0x0096CD10 - consume-then-operate ordering; no in-window hazard to the writer's already-completed read.

identity_observations.record_identity_content: NONE. The 12-byte record carries no resource ID, instance ID, parent or rotation channel. Rotation is a separate method call with a separate argument. (C6)
identity_observations.parent_attach_evidence: NONE in-window (C9). Candidates for next admission: 0x00509070 (SF method receiving getter-returned pointer - candidate SF+30/NiNode link setter), 0x00509190 (R5, arg=0), 0x006A34A0 (R3/R4 tail, this=[caller+8]).
identity_observations.resource_vs_instance_separation: Not observable in this package: no admitted instruction separates a resource ID from an instance ID. The only instance-shaped construction (R5's 0x130-byte record via 0x006C0D50 with lookup result) happens AFTER the position/rotation copy and its body is un-admitted.

stale_frame_variant_note: For R2/R3/R4 the record slot F+0x3C..F+0x47 has no in-body writer. If ALL preceding out-callees write fewer bytes than needed to reach the slot, the writer consumes stale frame bytes from a previous invocation of the same frame region. A shipped client feeding the SF position from garbage on every guard-taken path is functionally implausible, but this remains static variant V3 (not excluded by in-window evidence).
